description: A standalone Minecraft 1.21.1 Fabric mod overhauling enchanting. Enchanting you build toward, not a slot machine — five-stat shelves shape every roll, with treasure shelves, salvage tomes, and enchantment libraries. 75 enchantments. Part of the Concord collection.

mods.name: Meridian
mods.description: Zenith-style enchanting overhaul — stat-driven shelves, anvil tweaks, library storage, and tomes.

releases.notes:
Meridian 1.1.0 brings 26 new enchantments, permanently-unbreakable gear, and a
redesigned recipe-viewer browser, with clearer feedback across enchanting and a
bigger advancement tree. That takes Meridian to 101 enchantments in all.

*Requires Minecraft 1.21.1, Fabric Loader 0.16.10+, Fabric API 0.116.1+, and
Java 21.*

## Added
- **26 new enchantments** across six families — combat (Ambush, Pinpoint,
  Sunder, Trophy, Fortuity, Crescendo, Riposte, Joust), ranged and thrown
  (Longshot, Seeker, Harpoon), defense and mobility (Blink, Inexorable,
  Emberward, Reprieve, Loft), mining and tooling (Grind, Adamant, Reclaim),
  armor and shield (Hush, Decoy, Bastion, Everbloom), and tools and traversal
  (Timberfell, Grapnel, Thermal).
- **Tempered Core** — apply it at the anvil to make a tool, weapon, or piece of
  armor permanently unbreakable. There's a rare path to one: the Ender Dragon
  drops a Dormant Core, which you ignite into a Tempered Core at the enchanting
  table.
- **Everfull Flask** — an infused water bucket that never empties.
- **Everfeast rations** — infused food that feeds you many times over from a
  single inventory slot.
- **Anvil info pages** in EMI, REI, and JEI for the salvage and XP tomes, with
  matching tooltip lines on the tomes themselves.

## Changed
- **XP tomes now pay enchanting-table costs directly** — stored levels count
  toward an enchant and are spent alongside your XP bar, no withdrawing first.
- **Advancements are now usage-triggered**, unlocking as you actually use each
  system, with new anvil and stat branches guiding you deeper — 26 advancements
  in all.
- **Infusions browser redesign** in EMI, REI, and JEI — colored Eterna, Quanta,
  and Arcana stat bars replace grey requirement text, and each entry's hover now
  leads with the enchantment's description.
- **The craft slot is now distinct at rest** — when your shelves meet a recipe,
  it tints gold and previews the result and its XP cost without hovering.
- **Clearer feedback at the Enchantment Library and Filtering Shelf** — denied
  actions explain why on the action bar, and successful deposits play a sound
  and a particle puff.
- **More in-game teaching text** — purpose lines on every shelf tooltip, the
  stat formulas on the enchanting screen, and the point-doubling rule on the
  library slot.
- **Server config now syncs to clients** — enchantment and balance settings come
  from the host on join and `/meridian reload`, so everyone plays by the same
  rules.
- **New config toggles** to switch off duplication recipes, the Everfeast
  rations and Everfull Flask, and the Tempered Core system.

## Fixed
- A single misbehaving enchantment effect could break enchantment handling for
  every player for the rest of that game tick; each effect is now isolated so
  one failure can't cascade.
- Installing Meridian next to Tribulation no longer shows a spurious "update
  Tribulation" notice at startup. Meridian has never required Tribulation — the
  integration is optional and degrades cleanly against any version — but the mod
  metadata asked the loader to recommend a version that only existed as a
  prerelease.
- Meridian now accepts any Minecraft 1.21.x patch release rather than 1.21.1
  exactly, so a patch update no longer stops it from loading.

releases.notes:
This beta brings a massive wave of new enchantments across nearly every item type, rounding out the enchantment pool with dozens of additions — weapons, tools, armor, shields, elytras, mounts, tridents, ranged weapons, utility slots, and economy curses all got new options. A spyglass enchanting surface also makes its debut.

## Added

- **Weapon enchantments:** Reap, Mark, and Volley give melee and ranged weapons new tactical options.
- **Tool enchantments:** Kiln, Meticulous, Trailblaze, Dowse, and Twin Hook expand what your tools can do in the world.
- **Armor enchantments:** Winterward, Umbral, and Stormward add new defensive and elemental protections.
- **Shield enchantments:** Stagger and Bullrush turn your shield into an active threat.
- **Elytra enchantments:** Tailwind and Falconstrike make aerial traversal and diving attacks more powerful.
- **Mount enchantments:** Wavestride and Endurance improve riding in water and over long distances.
- **Trident enchantments:** Undertow and Torrent bring new aquatic combat and movement options to tridents.
- **Ranged enchantments:** Pin and Skyfall add crowd-control and aerial sniper play.
- **Utility enchantments:** Groom, Verdure, and Clearsight cover quality-of-life niches that were previously empty.
- **Economy enchantments:** Thrift and Alchemist's Draw reduce costs; Curse of Toll and Curse of Dissonance add new economic downsides to the curse pool.
- **Aquatic enchantments:** Ballast and Abyssal, plus the new Curse of Waterlogging, fill out the underwater kit.
- **Attunement** — a shelf-bound repair enchantment that links an item to a nearby shelf for passive mending.
- **Tracker's Lens** — the spyglass is now an enchantable item with its own enchantment surface.
- **Eleven new curses** fill gaps across item types that previously had no curse coverage.
- A `/meridian audit` command lets you inspect how third-party enchantments are registered alongside Meridian's own.

## Fixed

- Curse of Molting no longer causes a visible flicker when the fizzle effect is predicted client-side.

releases.notes:
Beta 1.1 is the enchantment content wave — 26 new enchantments across every combat and tool slot — plus a new unbreakable-item system, Everfeast rations, and a redesigned recipe-viewer experience.

## Added

- **26 new enchantments** spanning melee, ranged, armor, shields, mining, and traversal: Ambush, Pinpoint, Sunder, Trophy, Fortuity, Crescendo, Riposte, Joust, Longshot, Seeker, Harpoon, Blink, Inexorable, Emberward, Reprieve, Loft, Hush, Decoy, Bastion, Everbloom, Grind, Adamant, Reclaim, Timberfell, Grapnel, and Thermal.
- **Everfull Flask** and **Tempered Core** — a new unbreakable-item system. The Dormant Core drops from the Ender Dragon and is upgraded at the anvil.
- **Everfeast rations** — a new infusion for food items.
- **Tether** — a shared keep-on-death enchantment that integrates with the `#c:soulbound` tag, converging with other mods that use the same system.
- Enchantment descriptions now appear when hovering over books in EMI, REI, or JEI.
- The Infusions browser in EMI/REI/JEI has been redesigned with colored stat bars.
- Tooltip teaching text added to enchanting stats, shelves, and the library — hover anything to learn what it does.
- Anvil pages in EMI/REI/JEI now explain how tomes work with the anvil.
- XP tomes can now pay enchanting table costs directly without separate XP.
- The craft slot highlights visually when a recipe match is found.
- The advancement tree has been reworked with usage-triggered advancements and new anvil and stat branches.

## Changed

- Server config values now sync to connected clients automatically.
- Duplication recipes and Everfeast recipes can each be toggled off in the config.
- The Tempered Core system can be disabled in the config.

## Fixed

- The enchantment library and filtering shelf now show clear success and deny feedback when inserting or rejecting books.
- An error thrown by one enchantment's effect handler no longer interrupts other enchantments ticking on the same entity.
- The projectile bounce tracker no longer carries stale state across server restarts.

releases.notes:
Meridian 1.0.0 is the first stable release — a complete enchanting overhaul that
replaces the vanilla enchanting table's single "power" value with a five-stat
system, 25 themed shelf blocks, an enchantment library, salvage and XP tomes,
anvil upgrades, and 75 original enchantments.

## Added
- Stat-driven enchanting table — five stats (Eterna, Quanta, Arcana,
  Rectification, Clues) replace the vanilla power value. Eterna scales enchanting
  up to level 100, and higher stats bias toward rarer enchantments, steady
  results, and more preview hints.
- 25 themed shelf blocks across six tiers — from starter bookshelves to the
  Draconic Endshelf, the only way to reach Eterna 50. Each shelf feeds stats to a
  nearby table, and higher tiers are crafted at the table itself, so building your
  collection *is* the progression. Utility shelves add Clues, Rectification, an
  enchantment blacklist, and treasure rolls like Mending.
- Enchantment-table crafting — once your shelves meet a recipe's stat thresholds,
  the third enchant slot becomes a craft button for shelf upgrades, tome upgrades,
  Infused Breath, budding amethyst, echo shards, and more.
- Enchantment Library — a storage block that banks enchanted books into a
  per-enchantment point pool and dispenses them for XP. Upgrade the Basic Library
  to the Library of Alexandria to hold higher levels without losing stored books.
  Deposits accept hopper automation.
- Salvage tomes — the Scrap, Improved Scrap, and Extraction tomes move
  enchantments off an item in the anvil, each trading XP cost against how much you
  recover and whether the source item survives.
- XP tomes — three tiers of consumables that bank experience levels for later.
  Right-click to store a level, shift-right-click to withdraw one; a lime bar
  shows how full the tome is.
- Anvil upgrades — the Prismatic Web strips every curse from an item while keeping
  its other enchantments, and an iron block repairs a damaged anvil one tier.
- 75 original enchantments across combat, ranged, tools, mobility, mounts, elytra,
  and shields — including Excavate 3x3 mining, Prospect vein mining, Siphon,
  Stormcall, and Final Gambit.
- Warden Tendrils now drop from Wardens (a guaranteed one, with Looting raising
  the odds of a second) — the key material for Sculk-tier shelves.
- 18 advancements guiding progression from your first shelf to Eterna 50.
- Recipe-viewer and tooltip support out of the box — EMI, REI, and JEI show an
  Infusions crafting category and an Enchantments browser, and Jade surfaces shelf
  stats and library contents on hover.
- Inline enchantment descriptions (optional) — a short gray line under each
  enchantment in tooltips, the enchanting preview, and the library, covering all
  75 Meridian enchantments and every vanilla one.
- Server-tunable balance — override any enchantment's max level, loot level, cap,
  or availability, and retune every shelf's stat contribution, all applied live
  with `/meridian reload`.

releases.notes:
Beta 3 brings visual polish, tooltip improvements, and a handful of multiplayer fixes that were blocking a clean 1.0 launch.

## Added

- **Prismatic Web** enchantment now uses a fully animated glyph texture.
- The mod icon has been updated to a custom astrolabe glyph.
- Vanilla enchantments now display flavor descriptions in their tooltips, matching the style of Meridian's own enchantments.
- Loot drops that roll enchantments (mob equipment, chests, fishing) now go through Meridian's enchanting system, with proper max-level caps applied.
- A new `meridian:mob_equipment` tag lets datapack and modpack authors control which enchantments can appear on mob-worn gear.

## Fixed

- On dedicated servers, enchanting stats now correctly sync to clients on join — previously the server's stat registry was never sent, causing the enchanting table to behave as if no stats existed.
- The enchantment browser no longer briefly shows vanilla placeholder data while waiting for the server sync to arrive.
